STUDY 02 · MULTIMODAL LANGUAGE MODELS · MASTER'S THESIS

Affective Vulnerabilities
in Multimodal Language Models

From internal representations to generalisable image-only attacks.

Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct · visual evaluation · internal-state analysis · activation steering · universal adversarial perturbations.

01

Executive summary

  1. Interestingness is largely a property of the image, shared across personas.

    It is decodable in the vision encoder before persona information reaches the model. The same images also tend to stay high or low in interest across personas.

  2. Concept geometry predicts behavioural effects.

    At layer 29, the cosine similarity between a characteristic direction and the interestingness direction predicts how strongly steering it changes the final rating.

  3. Attacks on affective states transfer across tasks.

    Without retraining, stress shifts evaluation in the predicted severity direction, suggesting that the attack reaches a cognitive mode upstream of task level behaviour.

  4. The sum is not greater than its parts: personas are compositional.

    Stable, decodable characteristic vectors add together to predict where a combined persona's activation will end up.

  5. Targeted representation interventions can be recreated from pixels alone.

    Universal perturbations look like noise to people, but target particular internal directions and reproduce their behavioural effect without changing the prompt.

  6. Stress UAPs transfer across models.

    Preliminary results suggest that the relevant model geometry is similar enough for stress UAPs to transfer across model families.

02

From prompted state to model evaluation

Two persona prompts differ in exactly one feature but see the same image and rating request. Any difference in response or activation can therefore be attributed to that feature.

03

Interestingness is shared across personas

Personas modulate how interesting an image is rated, especially through emotion. But they do not appear to define interestingness from scratch: the same images tend to remain in high- and low-interest categories across persona conditions.

2.27 → 3.64Mean rating range across emotions, from male anger to female awe. The blank-persona mean is 2.75.
≤ 0.19Largest male–female gap for the same emotion. Female personas rate slightly higher in all eight pairs.
Awe and excitementThe only conditions with a visible share of “Very” and “Extremely Interesting” ratings.

Each bar is the share of the same 500 images assigned to each interestingness category. The distributions show systematic persona modulation; the repeated-image comparison is what shows that highly and weakly interesting images are largely shared across personas.

04

Interestingness appears before the persona

Interestingness is already readable from the image in the vision encoder, before any persona information is available. Persona characteristics become readable only after language integration; partial emotion structure also appears in the visual stream.

Shading marks the 34 vision layers; the remaining 48 layers are the language stream. The vision tower is a crucial contrast: prompt-defined identity controls stay near chance, while image-grounded interestingness is already decodable before persona integration.

This is in-sample projection separability, so it establishes decodable structure rather than causal importance or cross-task generalisation.

05

Personas are compositional directions

At the selected language layer, persona characteristics form stable, readable directions. Their linear sums predict the combined persona state: there is no evidence here that the whole persona requires an additional, irreducible representation.

06

Mid-layer geometry predicts behavioural influence

At layer 29, the cosine alignment between a characteristic direction and the interestingness-label direction predicts the slope of its later behavioural effect. This links a mid-layer geometric relation to a rating produced much later in the model.

07

From representation-specific intervention to pixels

A single pixel-space perturbation is optimised toward one causal internal direction, then added unchanged to held-out images. It looks like noise to people, but targets a specific representation and reproduces its behavioural effect without changing the prompt.

08

Affective states transfer upstream of task-level behaviour

The same state-targeted perturbation shifts damage, moral and shopping evaluations without retraining. Because the effect survives across different task formats, the working interpretation is that affective states sit upstream of task-level behaviour.

Cross-model transfer is currently running. Early workload and interestingness runs reproduce above-control effects in several Qwen and LLaVA task settings; remaining shuffled controls, bootstrap intervals and model runs will determine the final comparative claim.
